text: It's ten to ten. The Orion go/no-go review starts at ten, and the context is scattered across email, chats and files.
So instead of digging through your inbox, you open the Code tab in the Copilot app.
You describe the app once, in plain words: your calendar, a briefing for each meeting, and the rules it must follow.
Copilot plans the app, writes the code, and connects Outlook and Work IQ, using your own sign-in.
Before you see anything, it checks its own work: typecheck, lint, and a pre-deploy gate.
About fifteen minutes later, the preview opens on your real calendar. No sample data.
Settings show exactly which connectors the app can use. The app itself never sees your password or a token.
Select Publish, and the app runs on the Copilot Managed Runtime, with its own web address.
Each colleague who opens it approves the connections with their own account, so everyone sees only their own data.
And admins stay in charge: who pays for it, which connectors and actions it may use, and who it's shared with.
Now it's your turn. Open the lab, and build it yourself.
